chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Khalid ibn Muhammad Al-Asamm, who said:

A man entered the Sacred Mosque while in Ihram, so he entered into Tawaf wearing a shirt and a robe. The people came upon him, tearing his shirt, and he was firm (did not remove it). Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saw them handling his shirt and tearing it, so he said to him, 'What did you do?' He said, 'I entered Ihram like this, with the shirt and robe on.' He said, 'Remove it from your head; it is not removed from your feet. Rather, it was ignorance.' Then someone else came to him and asked him, saying, 'What do you say about a man who enters Ihram with a shirt on?' He said, 'He should remove it from his head.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who enters Ihram wearing a shirt and robe?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the common misconception that the shirt must be fully removed from the feet, clarifying that only the portion covering the head is removed while the lower part remains, as the prohibition specifically targets the head covering. This ruling highlights the distinction between the general prohibition of stitched garments and the specific requirements for Ihram attire, emphasizing that the garment's structure determines its permissibility rather than its complete removal. The incident underscores the practical application of fiqh principles in the context of Hajj rituals, where precision in ritual purity and attire is paramount.
